data.title: Boston's Iconic Sign Shines Again Over Kenmore Square
data.description:
Boston's Iconic Sign Shines Again Over Kenmore Square

Boston's Iconic Sign Shines Again Over Kenmore Square

PR Newswire

BOSTON, Nov. 20, 2026

CITGO Sign beams once more after public celebration of the only federally landmarked sign in Massachusetts, finishing the Kenmore Square Redevelopment Project

BOSTON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Boston's iconic CITGO Sign lit up the skyline again Thursday night as Mayor Michelle Wu, Secretary Phillip Eng and Boston City Councilor Sharon Durkan joined CITGO executives, community members, project partners and elected officials to gather in Kenmore Square for a community celebration and public relighting. The event marked the completion of the Sign's repositioning to its new home, the final phase of the Kenmore Square redevelopment project at 660 Beacon Street. The CITGO Sign, the only federally landmarked sign in Massachusetts, now sits 30 feet higher and 120 feet to the east on the roof of 660 Beacon Street, restoring the original viewsheds of the Sign in Boston's skyline.

"We've waited a long time to see the CITGO Sign light up again with our Kenmore Square neighbors and partners," said Karl Schmidt, vice president of supply and marketing at CITGO Petroleum. "The countdown took only seconds but getting there took years, and I want to thank everyone who made it possible for the CITGO Sign to shine over Boston again."

"The CITGO sign has been a quirky, beloved landmark for decades, signaling to residents and visitors that they are approaching the heart of Boston," said Mayor Michelle Wu. "Today, we celebrate its relighting, knowing that Bostonians will feel closer to home when they see it shining higher and brighter."

"The CITGO Sign is an iconic part of Boston's skyline and a symbol of Massachusetts that people across the country recognize," said Governor Maura Healey. "For generations, it has welcomed Red Sox fans to Fenway Park, guided Boston Marathon runners toward the finish line and served as a familiar sight for residents and visitors alike. It's wonderful to see this beloved landmark shining brightly once again, and I'm grateful to everyone who helped preserve this special piece of our history for generations to come."

"Under the leadership of the Healey-Driscoll Administration, we are proud to support this effort to recognize and preserve the sign as a historic landmark. We are grateful to partner and collaborate with our local, state and federal partners to make this important effort a reality. Preserving landmarks like the CITGO Sign also help to strengthen the vibrancy of our neighborhoods, celebrate the unique character and support the communities, local businesses and residents who make them special," said Interim Secretary of Transportation and MBTA General Manager Phil Eng.

"Kenmore Square is an important part of Boston's history and a vibrant part of its future," said Lieutenant Governor Kim Driscoll. "This project shows how we can preserve the landmarks that make our communities special while supporting new development and economic growth. Thank you to the community members, businesses and partners who worked together to bring this iconic sign back to life."

"Signs help us navigate our roads and connect us to the places we're going. Few signs, however, become landmarks in their own right," said Interim Highway Administrator Meghan Haggerty. "The CITGO Sign has done just that for generations of Bostonians and visitors, and we're proud to have helped preserve this iconic piece of Massachusetts history."

The public celebration on the Commonwealth Avenue Mall in Kenmore Square featured performances by the Boston University Pep Band and Berklee College of Music artists Kuper Walker, Ollie Mann, and dreamcorp – a first-time collaboration for the two schools. Representatives from the Kenmore Square Business Association, Suffolk, and the Boston Athletic Association participated in the speaking program and commemorative videos led into the official countdown, when the Sign was illuminated from its new position and permanent home above Kenmore Square.

CITGO Sign History and Background

The Sign's history at the site dates to 1940, when the original Cities Service sign was installed. The CITGO Sign debuted in 1965 and has been a familiar sight for generations of fans headed to Fenway Park and runners approaching the final mile of the Boston Marathon presented by Bank of America. The Federal Highway Administration and the Massachusetts Department of Transportation formally included the sign in their inventory of signs lawfully in existence before the adoption of the Highway Beautification Act of 1965, allowing for its preservation. The Sign also now includes a "Kenmore Square" belt sign highlighting its permanent home in the district.

"The CITGO Sign is an integral part of the identity of Kenmore Square and belongs to the generations who have grown up seeing it light up our skyline for more than 60 years. While CITGO may think of it as their sign, in Boston, we know it as ours," said Sharon Durkan, Boston City Councilor, District 8. "Its return is a celebration of our City's history and a testament to what we can accomplish when we come together to preserve the things that make our neighborhoods special. I'm thrilled to see this iconic Sign stand a little taller and shine over Kenmore Square once again."

"At Cornwall's, we've had a front-row seat to the changes in Kenmore Square over the years, and the CITGO Sign has been a constant through so much of it," said Pam Beale, president of the Kenmore Square Business Association and owner of Cornwall's. "Seeing it lit again tonight was a reminder of how much that familiar view means to the people who live and work here and we're grateful for everyone that helped get us to this moment."

CITGO Sign Repositioning Process

The repositioning project included construction of a new truss structure built into the existing anchor platform which was built into the core and roof of 660 Beacon Street. The Sign's new location restores the original sightlines that have defined its presence in Kenmore Square and Boston's skyline since its installation, as contemplated in the City's Article 80 review and approval of the larger Kenmore Square Development project.

Suffolk, the contractor of record, completed the repositioning of the CITGO Sign alongside partners, including: Related Beal, JCL Safety Services, Poyant, Principle Industries, Federal Heath, Liberty, Capco Steel Erection Co., JFS Roofing, Astro Crane, Maxim Crane Works, Sign Erection & Maintenance, GEI Consultants, Select Demo Services and Mcdonald Electrical Corporation.

"As a Boston-based builder, we understood both the significance of the CITGO sign to our city and the responsibility that came with moving it," said Pat Lucey, President of the Northeast and National Centers of Excellence at Suffolk. "This was a highly technical project in the heart of a busy neighborhood, and it took careful planning, precise engineering, and exceptional craftsmanship to get it right. I'm proud of our team and trade partners for their work and grateful to CITGO for trusting Suffolk with a Boston icon. Now, the next generation of fans, runners and neighbors can look up and make their own memories beneath that familiar glow."

ABOUT CITGO

CITGO Petroleum Corporation is a recognized leader in the refining industry and operates under the well-known CITGO brand. CITGO owns and operates three refineries located in Lake Charles, La.; Lemont, Ill.; and Corpus Christi, Texas, and wholly and/or jointly owns 43 active terminals, eight pipelines and three lubricants blending and packaging plants. With approximately 3,300 employees and a combined crude capacity of approximately 829,000 barrels-per-day (bpd), CITGO ranks as the fifth largest and is one of the most complex independent refiners in the United States. CITGO transports and markets transportation fuels, lubricants, petrochemicals and other industrial products, and supplies a network of approximately 4,000 locally owned and independently operated branded retail outlets. CITGO Petroleum Corporation is owned by CITGO Holding, Inc.

GREAT RAIL JOURNEYS INTRODUCES TWO NEW LANDMARK COLLECTION JOURNEYS FOR 2027 IMMERSING TRAVELERS IN EUROPE AND AFRICA

GREAT RAIL JOURNEYS INTRODUCES TWO NEW LANDMARK COLLECTION JOURNEYS FOR 2027 IMMERSING TRAVELERS IN EUROPE AND AFRICA

PR Newswire

CHICAGO, Nov. 20, 2026

From the Legendary Venice Simplon-Orient-Express to Rail-Inspired Experiences in South Africa, Great Rail Journeys Unveils Two Exceptional Escapes for Luxury-Minded Travelers

CHICAGO, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Great Rail Journeys (formerly Vacations By Rail) is introducing two new luxury experiences within its premium Landmark Collection: the exclusive Orient Express & Luxury Rhône Cruise itinerary and the immersive Premium South Africa: Kruger & Victoria Falls tour. Designed for travelers seeking exceptional accommodations, unforgettable experiences and seamless, expertly curated travel, the journeys showcase how rail can elevate luxury exploration, from Europe's most iconic train experiences to unique rail-inspired adventures in Southern Africa. Drawing on more than 50 years of expertise, Great Rail Journeys developed the Landmark Collection to feature iconic rail journeys, luxury accommodations and exclusive experiences that immerse travelers in the culture, history and landscapes of each destination.

One of the newest additions to the Landmark Collection is the 10-day Orient Express & Luxury Rhône Cruise with 2027 departures available from $19,995 per person. This exclusive itinerary, available only through Great Rail Journeys, begins with time in Venice before boarding the legendary Venice Simplon-Orient-Express for an iconic journey to Paris, followed by a luxury Rhône River cruise through southern France. Guests enjoy six nights aboard Belmond's elegant river vessel while discovering destinations including Lyon, Avignon and Arles. As the only travel company offering this unique combination of Belmond's renowned rail and river experiences, Great Rail Journeys provides travelers with a rare opportunity to seamlessly experience world-class dining, exceptional service and luxurious accommodations across two of Europe's most celebrated luxury journeys in a single vacation.

Also new to the Landmark Collection is the 10-day Premium South Africa: Kruger & Victoria Falls with 2027 departures available from $12,999 per person. Showcasing two of the continent's most remarkable destinations, the journey combines luxury accommodations, iconic wildlife encounters and unique rail-inspired experiences. Travelers enjoy premium safari experiences in world-renowned Kruger National Park in search of the Big Five while staying at the extraordinary Kruger Shalati, the renowned "train on the bridge" suspended above the Sabie River. The journey also includes an unforgettable five-course dinner aboard the elegant Royal Livingstone Express, where guests travel through the African bush in beautifully restored vintage railway carriages. Combined with time at Victoria Falls, one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World, the itinerary delivers a uniquely immersive exploration of Southern Africa.

Together, the two new Landmark Collection experiences showcase Great Rail Journeys' commitment to delivering extraordinary travel opportunities rooted in the company's rail heritage. Whether cruising through France aboard two iconic Belmond experiences or enjoying rail-inspired adventures in Southern Africa, guests can experience thoughtfully curated journeys designed to create lasting memories.

"These journeys exemplify what the Landmark Collection was created to deliver: extraordinary experiences that our guests simply can't find elsewhere," said Gary Crompton, Product Manager at Great Rail Journeys. "From our exclusive combination of the Venice Simplon-Orient-Express and a luxury Rhône cruise to unique rail-inspired experiences such as the Kruger Shalati and Royal Livingstone Express, every element has been carefully selected to create a truly memorable journey."

For more information about the Landmark Collection, visit greatrail.com/us/landmark or call (877) 929-7245. Follow Great Rail Journeys on Instagram and Facebook at @greatrailjourneys.us.

data.description:
Golden Key Group Selected by the City of Cleveland to Deliver Enterprise-Wide Management Training Program

Golden Key Group Selected by the City of Cleveland to Deliver Enterprise-Wide Management Training Program

PR Newswire

RESTON, Va., Nov. 20, 2026

GKG to design and execute tailored leadership development pathways for municipal people leaders, emerging talent, and executive officers.

RESTON, Va., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Golden Key Group (GKG), a leading provider of enterprise workforce solutions and human capital strategies, announced today that it has been selected by the City of Cleveland Department of Personnel and Human Resources to design and deliver its Citywide Management Training Program.

Under the contract, GKG will implement a comprehensive, cohort-based hybrid learning strategy aimed at driving leadership excellence across all municipal departments. The program leverages instructor-led sessions, digital LMS coursework, and applied capstone projects to strengthen core leadership competencies at every organizational tier.

"Every thriving city relies on leaders who are equipped to guide their teams through complex, evolving challenges," said Donnielle DeMesme, VP of Leadership and Development. "We are thrilled to partner with the City of Cleveland to bring our proven instructional design methodology and tailored training strategies to their workforce. This program is built to foster lasting culture change, elevate day-to-day operations, and empower Cleveland's public leaders at every stage of their career."

The GKG-designed curriculum includes three specialized tracks:

  • People Leaders Track: Supporting new and first-time managers through leadership transitions, coaching, conflict resolution, and communication.
  • Executive Leaders Track: Advancing emotional intelligence, culture building, and executive presence for directors and senior leaders.
  • Core Leadership Track: Equipping emerging leaders with essential skills in HR fundamentals, performance management, and team continuity.

This partnership highlights GKG's continued expansion in designing modern, outcome-driven learning solutions for state and local government agencies alongside its long-standing federal portfolio. Building on recent success with municipal and state initiatives including the City of Minneapolis and the Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM), GKG continues to solidify its position as a trusted learning and development partner for public sector organizations nationwide.

About Golden Key Group
Golden Key Group (GKG) is a premier provider of HR solutions, specializing in human capital management, employee training and development, and workforce strategy. Dedicated to excellence, integrity, and client-driven results, GKG partners with federal, state, and local government agencies to modernize their workforce, enhance operational efficiency, and cultivate strong leadership pipelines. Through customized, high-impact solutions, GKG equips public sector organizations with the strategic expertise needed to drive long-term success in an evolving employment landscape. For more information, visit www.goldenkeygroup.com.

data.title: Karviva Introduces Unwined Alcohol-Free Malbec and Rose Varieties
data.description:
ST. LOUIS, MO / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Karviva, a St. Louis beverage company, produces Unwined, an alcohol-free beverage range available in Malbec-inspired and Rose-inspired varieties. The products are made from fruit and botanicals rather than from wine that has been fermented and then dealcoholized.

The Malbec-inspired variety combines organic aronia, dark cherry, mulberry, prickly pear and schisandra berry. The Rose-inspired variety is made with organic white grape, cranberry, rosehip, ginger, schisandra, saffron and organic artichoke inulin. Both varieties are USDA Organic, contain no added sugar and are shelf-stable. The Malbec-inspired formula contains no grape juice. Karviva recommends chilling the beverages before serving.

The products are part of a beverage category that is drawing attention as drinking habits change. Gallup's 2026 Consumption Habits survey found that 54 percent of U.S. adults say they drink alcohol, matching the record low reported in 2025. The survey was conducted July 1-19, 2026. Gallup survey

Karviva produces its beverages at a facility in St. Louis. Founder Dr. Angela Zeng, Ph.D., MBA, a food scientist and Traditional Chinese Medicine scholar with training in pathology and biochemistry, established the facility after co-packers declined to produce her formulations.

"We developed Unwined as an alcohol-free beverage made from fruit and botanicals, with two distinct varieties," said Dr. Zeng. "The Malbec-inspired and Rose-inspired formulas reflect our decision to work from the ingredients themselves rather than from dealcoholized wine."

In 2025, Unwined received the Best Low/No Alcohol Beverage award at the World Beverage Innovation Awards, presented by FoodBev Media at drinktec in Munich. The awards announcement

About Karviva

Karviva is a beverage company founded by Dr. Angela Zeng, Ph.D., MBA, and based in St. Louis, Missouri. The company develops beverages using whole-plant ingredients, fruit, botanicals and hydroponically grown sprouts. Its product range includes Unwined, with Malbec-inspired and Rose-inspired varieties, as well as juice and Energy Juice products. Karviva products are made in St. Louis and are available in more than 2,000 retail locations nationwide. The company's beverages are made without added sugar or artificial sweeteners and are non-GMO.

Karviva's Energy Juice line received the 2025 ECRM Buyer's Choice Award, and the line was included in Progressive Grocer's 2026 Editors' Picks. These recognitions relate to the Energy Juice products, not Unwined. ECRM award information | Progressive Grocer's 2026 Editors' Picks

data.title: Canada Retail Sales Pull Back After 0.8% Rise in September — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart

OTTAWA--Canadian retail sales are heading for the sharpest drop in more than a year and a half, a possible sign of cracks in the resilience of household spending and slowing momentum for the economy.

The value of retail trade in the country increased 0.8% in September from the month before to a seasonally adjusted 75.31 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of about US$52.51 billion, Statistics Canada said Friday. That was a tick stronger than the 0.7% growth economists expected but was driven by a jump in how much drivers spent at the pumps.

An early tally of receipts indicates sales in October dropped 1.5%, which would be the steepest fall since February 2025.

Consumer spending in Canada remained solid through the third quarter, helping support economic growth. Retail sales rose 1.2% during the last quarter and volumes were up 1%, though sales volumes in September were up a slim 0.1%. The estimated weak start to the final quarter of 2026 could be even more pronounced in volume terms given seasonally-adjusted gasoline prices and goods prices generally were up slightly in October.

The Bank of Canada has projected economic growth will cool in the fourth quarter to below 1% annualized as the country adjusts to the latest U.S. tariffs, then recover next year. Economists say a string of soft data may point to even weaker growth, and undercut the case for further interest-rate increases near term.

"At this point, the likelihood of a hike in December is around 50-50, but diminishing," Charles St-Arnaud, chief economist at Servus Credit Union, said.

"Weakness in the economy in recent weeks suggests the Bank of Canada should pause to better assess the situation before hiking again, especially with some fuel prices easing recently," St-Arnaud said.

Statistics Canada provided no detail with its October estimate. The data agency's survey for September showed sales were up in five of the nine industry segments it tracks, led by trade at gas stations. Stripping out fuel, sales edged up 0.1 for the month.

Core sales, which strip out both fuel and motor vehicles and parts, similarly nudged up 0.1% for the month with a boost from general merchandise stores. Canadians also spent more on clothing, and on health and personal care but less at supermarkets and other grocery retailers.

"Once again, we're seeing a small uptick in Canadians' spending, but it hasn't really corresponded with them actually buying more," Jasleen Kaur Trehan, an economist at the Canadian Chamber of Commerce, said.

"September's retail numbers are again an example of how higher prices can make consumer spending look healthier than it really is," Kaur Trehan said. "With economic growth losing steam, a softer labor market and stubborn inflation squeezing purchasing power, households have less room to keep spending," she added.

The Bank of Canada's focus has turned to rising inflation risk, which prompted it to raise its policy interest rate in October for the first time in more than three years. Annual inflation has been at, or above, the upper end of the central bank's 1%-3% control range four months running, holding at 3.1% in October even as underlying measures of core inflation have remained more contained.

Statistics Canada's previous estimate of industry accounts suggested gross domestic product contracted 0.1% between August and September after essentially no change the previous two months, which would translate into annualized growth in the third quarter of 1.3% after a strong 3.8% expansion the quarter before. At the same time, employment in Canada has fallen three months running, driving the jobless rate in October to a six-month high of 6.7%.

"Today's data confirm that consumer spending will be a solid positive contributor to third-quarter GDP but also appear to signal that the slowing in growth seen late in the quarter and into the start of fourth quarter hasn't stemmed solely from sectors directly exposed to U.S. tariffs," Andrew Grantham, senior economist at CIBC Capital Markets, said.

Write to Robb M. Stewart at robb.stewart@wsj.com

(END) Dow Jones Newswires

data.title: 'Buyers are out for blood': With home sales at a record low, buyers are calling the shots
data.description:
By Aarthi Swaminathan

As home sales plummet, the housing market has taken another sharp turn in buyers' favor.

"I've never historically had trouble selling properties, and now there's just stuff that we can't sell," one real-estate agent said.

In mid-November in Kansas City, Mo., a homeowner called up real-estate agent Jeremy Applebaum, worried that their nearly $400,000 home wasn't selling. In the past six years, a home in that price range would have had over a dozen showings and been snatched up in 36 hours. But at that point, their house only had five showings even after being on the market for 60 days.

Applebaum wasn't surprised. More sellers are being forced to reduce their asking prices relative to the pandemic as they "get in line with reality," Applebaum told MarketWatch. "The consumer is less willing to pay whatever it takes to get a home now."

Even when buyers do make offers on homes, at this point, "sellers are just getting obliterated after inspections," he added. In one recent instance, the buyers walked away from the deal after the seller refused to make repairs to improve the home's condition.

About 15% of contracts signed to buy a home in October fell through, according to Redfin data, the highest share since April 2020.

"Nearly everybody is getting an inspection and buyers are just beating the sellers up," Applebaum said. "Buyers in some cases are out for blood and the sellers still think that they hold the upper hand when they really don't."

On Long Island, N.Y., real-estate agent Mia Rubin is also seeing buyers come down hard on sellers. At a recent home inspection for one home, the buyers flagged that the dryer wasn't getting hot enough. They wanted the seller to provide a credit for a replacement as a condition of the sale. Buyers are "nitpicking at a lot of things which in the past nobody would even mention," Rubin told MarketWatch.

One buyer wanted every electrical outlet in a house replaced or a credit to do it themselves after the inspection report found electrical-safety issues. Prospective buyers are also asking about "small" things, like whether there are carbon monoxide alarms in every bedroom, she said.

Buyers making extreme demands are a side effect of a housing market that seems to be hitting new lows. Home-buying demand has plunged over the last few months. In October, pending home sales, which refer to home transactions that are under contract but have not yet closed, fell to the lowest level since 2001, when the National Association of Realtors began tracking the figure. Existing-home sales that month fell to their lowest level since the financial crisis of 2008-09.

Meanwhile, mortgage rates have hovered above 7% for the past few months, adding hundreds of dollars a month in extra interest costs, and the median home price just hit another all-time high - two affordability obstacles driving many buyers out of the market.

In January 2026, a $2,000 monthly mortgage payment supported a home price $28,500 higher than a year earlier, noted Jake Krimmel, a senior economist at Realtor.com. By October 2026, that same $2,000 payment supported a home price $33,600 lower - a $62,100 swing - as mortgage rates rose over 7%.

Builders are also struggling to sell homes. In November, home-builder confidence fell to a 14-year low, with nearly half of builders offering price cuts to boost sales.

Jitters leading up to the midterm elections and the impact of the results may have also paralyzed some aspiring homeowners, Krimmel told MarketWatch, leading to lower demand and sales.

The few buyers left in the market are starting to call the shots, real-estate agents told MarketWatch.

Yes, some parts of the housing market continue to defy the rest of the nation. At one open house in Long Island over a recent weekend, 32 families attended, Rubin said, with four making offers for the three-bedroom, two-bath home. One offer was $75,000 over the asking price, which came "out of nowhere," Rubin said.

But many other parts of her market are less active. A two-bedroom condo she helped sell went for under the list price, something that would have been "unheard of" in the past, Rubin said. Buyers are also asking for more concessions following home inspections, she added.

In Kansas City, Applebaum also noted that parts of his market are still humming along, particularly at the upper end. A $900,000 home he helped sell got multiple offers, despite being far more expensive than the $400,000 home that was struggling to find buyers.

Luxury-home sales have been more resilient over the past year as wealthier buyers could afford them since they have more money.

But even in the wealthiest housing markets, pockets of distress are emerging.

In Los Angeles, real-estate agent Richard Schulman told MarketWatch that he's struggling to sell condos. Even though condos are a more affordable entry point for aspiring homeowners, high mortgage rates are pricing renters out. "You have to pay a huge premium over renting an apartment, so most buyers don't think there's a good justification," Schulman said.

With one West Los Angeles condo, price cuts weren't enough to attract buyers. The home is now listed at the price that another unit sold for in 2018. The house didn't have major issues, was not next to a freeway, and there were no concerns regarding its homeowners association or fees, Schulman said. It still wasn't selling.

"I've been doing this for 24 years. I've never seen anything like this," Schulman said.

"I've never historically had trouble selling properties, and now there's just stuff that we can't sell," he added. "Buyers have decided to stop buying and sellers have not adjusted pricing."

(Realtor.com is operated by News Corp subsidiary Move Inc.; MarketWatch publisher Dow Jones is also a subsidiary of News Corp.)

Do you have questions about real estate and home-buying that you would like to see covered in MarketWatch? We'd love to hear from you. You can write to us at readerstories@marketwatch.com. A reporter may be in touch to learn more. MarketWatch will not attribute your statements to you by name without your permission.

-Aarthi Swaminathan
